data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A decentralized network is more resilient to correlated failures if and only if it exhibits locally independent but globally non-amplifying failure modes; the evidence that distinguishes truly independent failures from hidden shared causes is whether interventions on a single node's failure rate predictably change the failure rates of geographically or architecturally distant nodes.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the decentralized network shares a common critical dependency (e.g., a shared DNS provider, a shared time sync protocol, or a shared cryptographic library) that affects the majority of nodes, then the network is not more resilient.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the large service has implemented effective isolation boundaries (e.g., bulkheads, cell-based architecture) that prevent internal failure propagation, then the centralized service may be more resilient due to coordinated response capacity.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the decentralized network lacks the coordination capacity to detect and respond to cascading failures, its theoretical independence may not translate to practical resilience.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Decentralized networks distribute failure modes across independent operational domains. Correlated failures in such networks can only occur through shared external dependencies (e.g., common cloud providers, shared libraries, common upstream supply chains). In contrast, large monolithic services, despite having more internal redundancy, create a single blast radius: internal coupling (shared state, configuration, deployment pipelines, network topologies) means that failures within one subsystem can propagate systemically. The distinguishing evidence is whether localized perturbations (e.g., taking a subset of nodes offline) produce a measurable change in the failure rates of distant, nominally independent nodes. If they do, the failures are not truly independent but share a hidden common cause.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
